Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the file. I pulled this into our pricing team and sketched three paths we typically offer for a commit uplift + price stability:

1) 12-month price hold + tiered uplift discount
   - Base commit: current price unchanged for 12 months.
   - Incremental commit (the +40%): applies a graduated discount (5% at +10%, 8% at +25%, 12% at +40%) tied to billing cadence.

2) Short-term bonus credits + longer-term price guard
   - One-off operational credit to reconcile March/April latency (we can formalize a $Xk credit).
   - 9–12 month price guard on per-token rates for your committed volume.

3) Aggressive commit swap (if youre willing to lock for 18 months)
   - Larger discount on incremental volumes and a burst pool for 5% overage at a reduced rate.

Id like to propose Option 1 as the starting point and include a small operational credit to close the latency item. If that sounds right I can circulate a one-page amendment and lock a time for Wed 10:00 PST or Thu 09:30 PST.

Draft attachment: GC_Master_Amendment_v3.pdf (term sheet stub)

—Mateo

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call Wednesday. Per our discussion, heres the formal proposal were prepared to put to contract: 

Proposal highlights:
- Term: 12 months (renewal effective 2027-07-01).
- Commit uplift: +40% to existing committed token volume.
- Pricing: current per-token rate held flat for the committed base and uplifted bands for 12 months; incremental discount on uplifted volume as follows: +10% => 5% discount, +25% => 8% discount, +40% => 12% discount.
- Operational credit: one-time $12,500 credit to address March/April incidents (applied as contra to next invoice).
- Overage handling: a 3-month grace period after Q3 launch — overage usage will be billed at list rate and eligible for credit within the subsequent invoice period up to the grace amount.
- Additional: 30-day SLA review clause; addendum for SOC2 evidence already provided.
